finding.title: Split tool/seed/lib/sefaria_mongo.dart (542), tool/seed_content_db.dart (809), tool/validate_seed_coverage.dart (401) under AG-3's 400-line cap

evidence.quote: // Comprehensive validator for the bundled content.db seed.

finding.why: AG-3 caps hand-written Dart files at 400 lines (generated files exempt); `wc -l` confirms these three are 542, 809, and 401 lines respectively, none carrying a generated-code header. seed_content_db.dart in particular interleaves CLI parsing, calendar generation, content-hash computation, xz orchestration, and DB validation in one file along its own '// ── Phase N ──' comment seams — a natural Extract-Class/Extract-File split once the AG-3 checker exists.
finding.recommendation: Split each file along its existing section markers once tooling for AG-3 lands: seed_content_db.dart along its '// ── Phase N ──' comments; sefaria_mongo.dart into ref-parsing vs. navigation/collection vs. index-loading modules; validate_seed_coverage.dart into report-formatting vs. diff-computation.
acceptance_criteria: wc -l on all three files reports ≤400
Once the pending AG-3 checker lands, these three files pass it

finding.title: Log the caught exception at 7 silent/overbroad catch sites across tool/ fetch-and-resolve helpers
finding.rule: EH-3 (log-less catch) / EH-4 (Error-subtype catch) — general lens applied to tool/
finding.why: None of these seven catch/except blocks log the caught error before discarding it — Dart sites return a generic error flag, Python sites `pass`/`continue`/`return None`. When a fetch or ref-resolution genuinely fails, the operator sees only an aggregate 'N errors'/'SKIP' count, never why (network error vs. malformed data vs. a real bug in the resolver itself), making failures expensive to diagnose. verify_seed_calendar.dart:202 additionally catches `Object` — broader than even `Error` — so it would also swallow a `TypeError`/`RangeError` from a bug in the tool's own JSON-parsing code and silently retry it up to 4 times before reporting the day as a generic 'live fetch failed', masking a real programming defect as a transient network blip.
finding.recommendation: Add a log line (print/stderr.writeln/sys.stderr.write) with the caught exception's message and ref/date context at each of the 7 sites before falling through to the existing error-flag return. Narrow verify_seed_calendar.dart:202's `on Object` to the specific exception types the HTTP client/JSON decoder can actually throw.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 7 cited sites logs the caught exception before returning its existing failure value
verify_seed_calendar.dart:202 no longer catches bare Object

finding.title: Add automated unit tests for sefaria_mongo.dart's ref/address-parsing engine (currently zero, only a manual eyeball script)
finding.rule: Feathers testability lens (TQ-1/TQ-8 spirit applied to tool/)

evidence.quote: /// Validates the Mongo ref→text resolution on the required sample refs.

finding.why: sefaria_mongo.dart implements longest-prefix title matching, schema-node walking with boundary rules, Talmud daf→array-index arithmetic (2a→2, 2b→3, 3a→4…), multi-section range flattening, and cross-version segment-wise text merging — 542 lines that decide exactly which Hebrew/English text a child sees for any given ref. `find test/tool -type f` returns only android_manifest_deep_links_test.dart, audit_and_arb_parity_test.dart, build_cities_db_admin1_test.dart, and schema_check_test.dart — none touch this file, and a repo-wide grep for 'SefariaMongo'/'sefaria_mongo' under test/ returns nothing. The only check is tool/seed/sample_validate.dart, a 34-line script that prints 9 hardcoded refs for a human to eyeball against a live local Mongo; it asserts nothing, isn't wired into make ci/make seed, and a regression in, say, the Talmud `(daf-1)*2+amud` formula would silently ship the wrong daf's text to every user of that program unless a human happens to notice the printed output looks off.
finding.recommendation: Add a unit-test file exercising SchemaNode walking, the Talmud daf-index formula, range flattening, and version-priority merge-first-non-empty against small in-memory fixtures (SefariaMongo's dependency is a concrete mongo_dart Db, but the pure helper methods — _parseTuple, _addressToIndex, _collectAddressed, _flatten — can be tested directly without a live connection).
acceptance_criteria: A new test file exercises: Talmud daf→index (2a→2, 2b→3, 3a→4), a multi-section range flatten, longest-prefix title matching against a comma-bearing child title, and version-priority merge-first-non-empty, using fixture data with no live Mongo
That test runs green under `dart test`/`flutter test` without Docker/Mongo present

finding.title: Decode xz's stderr before interpolating it in seed_content_db.dart's failure message (currently prints a raw byte list)
finding.why: Process.runSync is called at line 312-317 with `stderrEncoding: null`, so ProcessResult.stderr holds raw bytes (a Uint8List), not a decoded String. String-interpolating it at line 319 invokes List.toString(), producing something like 'xz failed: [120, 122, 58, 32, ...]' instead of xz's actual human-readable stderr text — exactly when a maintainer most needs a readable error, during a failing release build.
finding.recommendation: Pass `stderrEncoding: systemEncoding` (or explicit `utf8`) to this Process.runSync call, or explicitly `utf8.decode(xzResult.stderr as List<int>)` before interpolating it into the thrown StateError.
acceptance_criteria: Triggering an xz failure (e.g. temporarily pointing dbPath at a nonexistent file, or aliasing xz unavailable) prints a human-readable message, not a numeric byte-list
seed_content_db.dart's xz Process.runSync call sets stderrEncoding to a real Encoding, or decodes stderr before use

finding.title: Gate deploy-play-store.yml on a passing CI run for the exact SHA being deployed
finding.why: deploy-play-store.yml has no `needs:`/`workflow_run:` dependency on ci.yml and no step that checks the target SHA's check-run status. Its only steps between checkout and Play Store upload are checkout, codegen, and `flutter build appbundle --release` — no `flutter test`, `dart analyze`, `make audit`, or firestore-rules check. A maintainer who tags a commit that never went through review/CI (an emergency hotfix, a stale local branch, the wrong SHA) or whose ci.yml run is still red/in-progress can ship straight to Google Play production with nothing in the committed config to stop it — the only backstop is human diligence, which is exactly the kind of implicit, non-deterministic gate Rule 0 says not to rely on.
finding.recommendation: Add a job that queries the GitHub Checks API for the deploying SHA's required workflows before the build/upload steps run (or trigger deploys via a `workflow_call` from a successful ci.yml run instead of independent `push: tags`/`workflow_dispatch` triggers).
acceptance_criteria: deploy-play-store.yml fails fast if the deploying SHA has no green ci.yml run, before any build/signing steps execute.
A dry run against a SHA with a failing/missing CI run demonstrates the new gate blocking the deploy.
